questions.q: In the Meridian Outfitters scenario, which detail is a hidden constraint rather than a headline requirement?
options: That the three regional IT teams barely coordinate and none of the orgs has been through a data-quality cleanup
The nine-month deadline tied to the holiday launch
The requirement for a single global storefront
The requirement for real-time inventory visibility
questions.explain: The organizational and data-quality detail only surfaces when the CIO is asked privately — it isn't in the headline business requirements, which is exactly what makes it a hidden constraint a design has to account for anyway.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend NOT merging the three regional orgs within the nine-month window?
options: Because Salesforce technically prevents merging more than two orgs at once
Because the deadline, the lack of coordination between teams, and years of uncleaned data make a full merge the higher-risk path for this specific timeline
Because org consolidation is architecturally impossible on the current platform
Because leadership explicitly forbade any future org consolidation
questions.explain: Nothing technically blocks org consolidation — the recommendation is a risk call based on the specific combination of deadline, uncoordinated teams, and data quality, not a platform limitation.

questions.q: What role does the Data Cloud-based customer-profile layer play in the recommended design?
options: It replaces all three regional orgs entirely
It is only used for marketing email sends, not for the storefront
It resolves and unifies the customer identity across the three orgs without requiring any of them to migrate or merge data first
It stores the authoritative inventory count for all regions
questions.explain: The profile layer solves the unified-customer-view requirement independently of org consolidation, which is exactly what lets the team meet the deadline without betting it on a risky merge.

questions.q: Why does the design use published inventory-change events between regions instead of having the storefront query each regional org's database directly and synchronously?
options: Direct synchronous queries across orgs are not possible on any platform
Events are always faster than any synchronous call
Synchronous queries would violate Salesforce's terms of service
A direct synchronous cross-org dependency creates a shared failure point during the platform's highest-traffic season, which the event-driven approach avoids
questions.explain: The reasoning is about risk and resilience during peak load, not a technical impossibility — a hard synchronous dependency between regions during the busiest season is a fragile design choice regardless of raw speed.

questions.q: A review-board panelist asks, "Why didn't you just merge the three orgs like leadership asked for?" What is the strongest response based on this lesson's approach?
options: "Leadership didn't really mean that, so I ignored it"

"The actual business commitment is the storefront, unified profile, and inventory visibility by the deadline — a full merge inside nine months, given the data quality and team coordination issues, was the higher-risk way to deliver that commitment, and the design keeps a later, better-governed merge available as a follow-on"
"Merging orgs is against Salesforce best practice in every case"
"There wasn't enough time to consider alternatives"
questions.explain: This response directly addresses the panelist's challenge by naming the underlying business goal, the specific risk factors that ruled out a literal merge on this timeline, and the fact that consolidation remains possible later — the defensible pattern this lesson teaches.
